sampling_model.design: Two-fold cross-fitting under i.i.d. sampling from \(P\in\mathcal P_4\).
sampling_model.overlap: Censoring follow-up satisfies \(G_a(t\mid x)=(1-t)^2g_a(t,x)\) and vanishes at the fixed horizon.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Treatment propensity, event hazard, and rescaled censoring residual are unknown and learned foldwise by the endpoint local-cubic handle; no estimator-side rate is assumed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 4 gives a cross-fitted asymptotic-linear survival estimator under a uniform censoring floor and high-level nuisance product rates, and Section 5.3 obtains RMST inference by integration.
Theorem A1 gives a Gaussian limit for an unadjusted Kaplan--Meier RMST integral at the support endpoint under a finite weighted tail integral.
The paper develops efficient covariate-adjusted RMST estimation for randomized trials at an ordinary fixed follow-up horizon.
Theorem 1 gives whole-support local-polynomial conditional-density rates under nondegenerate local information and a smooth positive design density.
Theorem 3.2 gives pointwise asymptotic normality for local-polynomial Nelson--Aalen hazard smoothing strictly below the upper support boundary.
Self-normalized Gaussian approximation for independent sums is available under finite \(2+\delta\) moments.

body.tldr: In a designed-depletion or calibrated loss-to-follow-up regime, the censoring time is the earlier of two conditionally independent continuous loss or availability times whose near-horizon survivals vanish linearly, giving the known quadratic endpoint order while leaving the smooth residual censoring law unknown. At the scientific horizon, this quadratic censoring makes the influence function for survival itself non-square-integrable, but the remaining-life factor in fixed-endpoint RMST cancels one endpoint power and leaves a finite efficiency bound. The paper constructs a total cross-fitted one-step estimator that attains that bound uniformly over the stated radius-20 Hölder primitive class while learning the treatment propensity, event hazard, and rescaled censoring residual. Simultaneous local-cubic concentration in the last time--covariate cells gives nuisance rate \((\log n/n)^{1/3}\), and a terminal-strip Fano packing proves a matching minimax sup-norm lower bound for learning the event hazard over the same primitive class. This sharp primitive rate, exact product drift, weak \(5/2\)-moment Studentization, canonical-gradient certificate, and uniform Wald coverage form the publishable kernel.

project_justification.gap: Westling et al. establish machine-learning inference for treatment-specific survival and integrated RMST under a censoring floor and high-level nuisance-rate conditions. Classical endpoint Kaplan--Meier theory permits vanishing follow-up for integrated functionals but has no conditional confounding adjustment or learned nuisance blocks. Existing local-polynomial hazard theory does not supply uniform last-cell concentration when the predictable risk set collapses quadratically.
project_justification.niche: The nonempty niche is a fixed-target efficiency theorem on a primitive smooth class where survival-at-endpoint inference is irregular, RMST remains regular, the nuisance fits must preserve the known quadratic factor, and the feasible score may lack a third moment.
project_justification.fill: The project integrates the survival score before analysis, learns the smooth event hazard and \(q_a=S_ag_a\) by boundary-adaptive cubic risk-set equations, proves their terminal-cell \((\log n/n)^{1/3}\) rate without assuming it, and matches the event-hazard upper rate by a same-class terminal-strip Fano lower bound. It then propagates the exact product drift through cross-fitting and proves variance consistency and a uniform Studentized limit from a \(5/2\)-moment envelope.

body.related_work: Westling, Luedtke, Gilbert, and Carone (2024) is the writing and estimation exemplar: its Introduction moves from confounding and dependent censoring to a cross-fitted doubly robust survival estimator; Theorem 4 and Supplementary Lemmas 1--3 supply the foldwise decomposition and exact drift that are adapted here. Its condition B2 requires censoring survival bounded away from zero through the horizon, and Section 5.3 derives RMST inference by integrating the resulting survival-process limit. Tian et al. (2020), Theorem A1, and Stute (1995) show that an integrated Kaplan--Meier target can retain a Gaussian endpoint limit under a weighted tail integral; they neither adjust for covariates nor estimate conditional causal nuisances. Díaz et al. (2019) establish efficient covariate-adjusted RMST estimation in randomized trials with ordinary follow-up. Cattaneo et al. (2024), Theorem 1 and Appendix A.5, provide normalized local-polynomial bases, boundary-uniform Gram control, and Bernstein covering arguments under nondegenerate i.i.d. information. Jiang and Doksum (2003), equations (2.5)--(2.8) and Theorems 3.2 and 3.4, provide the Nelson--Aalen local-polynomial algebra but restrict asymptotics below an upper boundary with positive risk. Fan and Guerre (2016) provide whole-support polynomial reproduction and boundary matrix geometry, although their smooth design-density condition must be replaced by a direct density-band sandwich. Munch et al. (2024), Theorem 9 and Corollary 13, give integrated conditional-hazard rates for highly adaptive lasso under positive endpoint follow-up. Efromovich (2024) gives sharp mean-integrated-squared-error theory for conditional hazard estimation under right censoring, not simultaneous endpoint sup-norm control. Jing, Shao, and Wang (2003) supply the weak-moment self-normalization template, while Chernozhukov et al. (2018) supply foldwise conditioning and orthogonal product-remainder organization. Searches through September 11, 2026 found no result combining fixed-endpoint causal RMST efficiency, quadratic conditional follow-up loss, primitive learned-nuisance rates, and uniform feasible Studentization.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The decisive terminal-cell kill test is discharged by thm:primitive-endpoint-concentration. Its proof establishes an at-risk Gram of order \(Mh_M^4\), preserves coercivity under an arbitrary measurable density \(f\), controls the martingale numerator and Taylor remainder simultaneously, and makes low-count fallbacks uniformly negligible. Formalization must preserve those coupled bounds; weakening them to an \(n^{-1/4}\) nuisance rate would no longer imply the headline expansion. Numerical values from the presolve witness are diagnostics and are not theorem claims.
body.honest_scope: Identification of the fixed contrast is standard. Estimation and inference at the quadratic endpoint are resolved here for the stated primitive class. The theorem fixes the horizon \(1\), censoring exponent \(2\), one-dimensional covariate, smoothness order \(4\), and all radius and band constants. Within this class, the learned event-hazard sup-norm rate \((\log n/n)^{1/3}\) is minimax sharp; the converse does not claim a minimax lower bound for RMST risk or for each other nuisance separately. The result does not cover an estimated endpoint exponent, a shorter moving horizon, a parametric hazard subclass, or a different target. As an in-class sanity check, fix \(\delta\in(0,1)\), set \(\tau:=1-\delta\), and diagnostically restrict the same factor-preserving learner and score integrals to \([0,\tau]\). Every \(P\in\mathcal P_4\) then obeys \(G_a(t\mid x)\ge\delta^2/2\) on \([0,\tau]\), so the construction is compared in the ordinary positive-follow-up regime covered by Westling et al. (2024), while retaining its factor-preserving algebra. This diagnostic restriction is only a sanity check and does not change the fixed horizon-\(1\) target or introduce a censoring-floor assumption into the main result. The general censoring-exponent phase diagram remains a separate flagship question.
